questions.def: The reduced clause implies the subject is the same in both parts.
questions.question: Having finished the report, ___ it to my manager.

questions.def: 'Having + past participle' indicates an action completed before the next one.
questions.question: ___ the presentation, she felt relieved.

questions.def: Use present participle to show the reason for the main clause action.
questions.question: ___ the risks, he proceeded with the plan.

questions.def: 'According to' correctly introduces the source of the information.
questions.question: ___ the company's policy, employees must attend the training.

questions.def: Use the past participle because the document was acted upon (passive).
questions.question: The document, ___ yesterday, is now available online.

questions.def: Use 'seen' to indicate the city was passively observed.
questions.question: ___ from the hilltop, the city looked magnificent.

questions.def: Reduced adverbial clause requires only the adjective after 'although'.
questions.question: Although ___, she persevered and finished the marathon.

questions.def: 'Left' implies a passive action; the flowers were left to wilt.
questions.question: ___ in the sun, the flowers quickly wilted.

questions.def: Better to use 'As' instead of 'Being' at the start of the sentence.
questions.question: Being a good student, he always studied hard.

questions.def: 'Equipped' is correct as the soldiers were passively equipped.
questions.question: The soldiers, ___ with advanced technology, were ready.

questions.def: 'Using' indicates an active action of utilizing the software.
questions.question: ___ the new software, I found it very user-friendly.

questions.def: 'Having considered' implies the consideration happened before verdict.
questions.question: ___ the evidence, the jury reached a verdict.

questions.def: 'Surprised' is the correct passive participle here.
questions.question: ___ by the news, she remained calm.

questions.def: 'Being' introduces a reason or characteristic.
questions.question: ___ a doctor, he is qualified to give medical advice.

questions.def: 'Written' indicates the book was passively written.
questions.question: The book, ___ by a famous author, became a bestseller.

questions.def: 'Motivated' describes their passive state of being driven.
questions.question: ___ by success, they worked tirelessly.

questions.def: 'Considering' introduces the reason for postponement.
questions.question: ___ all the factors, we decided to postpone the event.

questions.def: 'Submitted' acts as a passive participle modifying 'report'.
questions.question: The report, ___ last week, is now being reviewed.

questions.def: Use 'As it was raining' rather than 'Being rain'.
questions.question: Being rain, the match was cancelled.

questions.def: 'Informed' indicates the staff were passively informed.
questions.question: ___ of the change, all staff were notified.

questions.def: Requires a passive participle after 'unless'.
questions.question: Unless ___ otherwise, the meeting will be held on Friday.

questions.def: 'Having read' indicates completion before assembling.
questions.question: ___ the instructions carefully, he assembled the furniture.

questions.def: Better to use 'Having had' because 'had to wait' is the meaning.
questions.question: Having to wait, I was bored.

questions.def: 'Invited' shows she was passively invited.
questions.question: ___ to the party, she felt very happy.

questions.def: 'Following' implies the presentation happened before answering.
questions.question: ___ the presentation, he answered questions from the audience.

questions.def: 'Completed' indicates the project was passively finished.
questions.question: The project, ___ on time, was a success.

questions.def: Reduced clauses need a subject if it's different from main clause.
questions.question: Having finished the exam, ___ home.

questions.def: Past participle reduces relative clause: which was submitted.
questions.question: The report, ___ yesterday, contained vital information.

questions.def: Past participle reduces relative clause: who was known.
questions.question: ___ for his expertise, he was consulted often.

questions.def: 'Despite' replaces 'although there was'.
questions.question: ___ the rain, the match continued.
